members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: Both rework `RequestResponder.cancel()` in src/mcp/shared/session.py — the exact same code block that currently sends an 'error response to indicate cancellation'. #2493's diff deletes that block outright (server.py's matching change is just a comment/log-text rename around logic that was already returning early). #2514's diff shows a distinct, adjacent hunk in the same method (dropping a stale `# pragma: no cover` on the entry-check, right where #2493's hunk begins) and adds a `CancelledNotificationParams` import, indicating it replaces the same send-on-cancel code with a real `notifications/cancelled` emission rather than deleting it. Both are targeting the same root issue: cancel() sends the wrong (or no) message when a request is cancelled, in violation of the spec's 'receivers must not send a response for a cancelled request' rule.

Both are targeting the same root issue: cancel() sends the wrong (or no) message when a request is cancelled, in violation of the spec's 'receivers must not send a response for a cancelled request' rule. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs touch the identical two raise sites in auth/utils.py plus session.py, so they'll conflict on merge. #2565's change to those two lines is a strictly additive one-liner (`... from e` appended, original f-string message with embedded `{e}` left intact), whereas #2777 additionally rewrites the exception message text itself (drops the interpolated `{e}` from the message, e.g. `"Invalid registration response"` instead of `f"Invalid registration response: {e}"`), which is a behavior change beyond exception chaining and a larger diff footprint that risks breaking anything asserting on exact message content.
